name: Japan

kings.title: Prince Shōtoku
kings.biography: Semi-legendary regent of the Asuka period who authored Japan's Seventeen-Article Constitution, championed Buddhism, and established official diplomatic ties with Sui dynasty China.

kings.title: Minamoto no Yoritomo
kings.biography: Founder and first Shogun of the Kamakura Shogunate, establishing feudal military supremacy in Japan that endured for nearly seven centuries.

kings.title: Oda Nobunaga
kings.biography: The Great Unifier of Sengoku-era Japan, revolutionizing warfare with massed arquebus volley tactics, conquering central Japan before his betrayal at Honno-ji.

kings.title: Toyotomi Hideyoshi
kings.biography: Second Great Unifier who rose from peasant foot soldier to Imperial Regent (Kampaku), enforcing nationwide sword hunts, land surveys, and building Osaka Castle.

kings.title: Tokugawa Ieyasu
kings.biography: Master strategist and founder of the Tokugawa Shogunate, achieving decisive victory at the Battle of Sekigahara in 1600 and securing over 250 years of peaceful Edo rule.

sites.name: Tōdai-ji Temple & Great Buddha
sites.description: Historic Buddhist temple complex in Nara housing the Daibutsu (Great Bronze Buddha), one of the largest wooden buildings in the world.

sites.name: Himeji Castle (White Heron Castle)
sites.description: Japan's most pristine surviving feudal castle, featuring an intricate defensive maze of gates, walls, and brilliant white plaster architecture.

sites.name: Kinkaku-ji (Golden Pavilion)
sites.description: Iconic Zen Buddhist temple in Kyoto covered in pure gold leaf, reflecting seamlessly across the Kyoko-chi mirror pond.
